record.original_question: Construct a system of scalar invariants of a projective structure that vanish if and only if there exists (locally, in a neighborhood of almost every point) a metric compatible with a given projective structure.

evidence.quote: Construct a system of scalar invariants of a projective structure that vanish if and only if there exists (locally, in a neighborhood of almost every point) a metric compatible with a given projective structure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge 2$. A projective structure on $M$ is an equivalence class $[
abla]$ of torsion-free affine connections, where two connections $
abla$ and $\widetilde
abla$ are equivalent if they share the same unparametrized geodesics; equivalently, there exists a $1$-form $\Upsilon$ such that
$$\widetilde
abla_X Y = 
abla_X Y + \Upsilon(X)Y + \Upsilon(Y)X$$
for all vector fields $X,Y$. A pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is said to be compatible with $[
abla]$ if its Levi-Civita connection belongs to the projective class $[
abla]$.

A scalar invariant of a projective structure is a smooth function on $M$, built polynomially from the components of a representative connection $
abla\in[
abla]$ and their finite-order partial derivatives, that is independent of the choice of representative in the projective class (equivalently, transforms as a scalar under the projective transformations above) and is independent of the choice of local coordinates.

Construct an explicit finite system of such scalar invariants $\{I_1,\dots,I_N\}$ of an arbitrary projective structure $[
abla]$ on $M$ with the following property: for almost every point $p\in M$, the projective structure $[
abla]$ admits a compatible pseudo-Riemannian metric on some neighborhood of $p$ if and only if
$$I_1 \equiv I_2 \equiv \cdots \equiv I_N \equiv 0$$
on a neighborhood of $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved in low dimensions. In dimension 2, an explicit scalar projective invariant of order 5 (with two further order-6 invariants in the generic real-analytic case) characterizes metrizability (Bryant–Dunajski–Eastwood). In dimension 3, projectively invariant tensorial obstructions algebraic in the projective Weyl curvature have been constructed. A complete, fully general system of scalar invariants giving a sharp local generic metrizability criterion in arbitrary dimension does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Metrisability of two-dimensional projective structures
status_evidence.snippet: An explicit local obstruction to the existence of a Levi-Civita connection within a given projective structure on a surface, of order 5 in the components of the connection and expressible as a weighted scalar projective invariant.
status_evidence.claim: Dimension 2 case solved by an order-5 scalar projective invariant plus two order-6 invariants in the generic case.

status_evidence.title: Metrisability of three-dimensional path geometries
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit obstructions to the local existence of a Levi-Civita connection in a 3-dimensional projective class are given by projectively invariant tensors algebraically built from the projective Weyl curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Dimension 3 obstructions known as projectively invariant tensors built from projective Weyl curvature.

status_evidence.title: Metrics in Projective Differential Geometry: The Geometry of Solutions to the Metrizability Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Metrics in the projective class correspond to maximal rank solutions of a projectively invariant overdetermined PDE (the metrizability equation), studied via prolongation and tractor calculus.
status_evidence.claim: General framework reduces metrizability to an overdetermined invariant PDE; full scalar-invariant criterion in all dimensions not given.
